turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... I just can't stop thinking about my appearance. I work as a host at a restaurant, and I'm constantly fixated on my hairline and how my face looks, especially under the harsh lights in the dining room. I just feel like they make me look really old and... strange. It takes up a lot of my thoughts. My coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about at all, but I just can't stop focusing on it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports being constantly fixated on perceived flaws in their hairline and face that their coworkers do not observe.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself performing any specific actions, like checking your reflection in mirrors or grooming yourself excessively, to try to fix or hide these features?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. Um, especially right before a shift. I'll just keep checking the bathroom mirror over and over. I take pictures on my phone from different angles to try to see exactly what I look like, and I'm always combing my hair forward to try and hide my hairline. I just keep replaying in my head how the guests might see me when I walk up to them. Honestly, it takes up so much time that I end up being late, or I get so worked up I can barely bring myself to go out to the front stand.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors such as repeatedly checking the mirror, taking photos from different angles, and combing hair forward to hide their hairline.
